Hi David / team,

Thanks again for the demo yesterday — the platform looks great and we9re keen to kick off a 6-week pilot covering two regional depots. - Requested discount: 35% one-time pilot credit

Thanks David — quick context from ops side: Greenleaf looks like a solid pilot (logistics ops use-case, good reference potential). Typical guidance: pilot discounts up to 25% can be approved by Sales Ops for <90 day pilots; anything beyond 25% routes to Deal Desk/Finance.

I9m attaching the price_approval_form.xlsx with the required fields filled (estimated ARR if converted, expected reference value, and suggested revenue tag). If Deal Desk approves, we should set the Salesforce stage to "Commit - pilot approved" so FP&A includes the upside as a contingent commit for Q2.

From: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.com>

Cc: Maya Ranganath <procurement@greenleaflogistics.com>
Date: Wed, 10 Mar 2027 12:43:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Greenleaf pilot pricing ask - expedited approval needed

David / Vanessa / Maya — thanks for the details. Quick decision from Deal Desk: we cannot approve 35% as-is. Approve up to 20% for a 6-week pilot with the following guardrails:

- Discount capped at 20% (one-time credit applied to pilot invoice)
- Contractual term: explicit pilot SOW + success criteria; conversion conversation before pilot end
- Revenue tagging: mark as "Pilot - contingent" in SFDC; include expected conversion probability at 40% for FP&A forecasting purposes
- Customer to provide PO within 10 business days of signature; finance requires invoice terms 30 days net

Impact to forecast: approving 20% will reduce recognized committed value for Q2 by approximately $10.8k (on the pilot line). If we tag as "contingent commit" at 40% conversion, FP&A should model ~$17k of expected revenue into Q2 figures rather than the full list price.

I9ve uploaded our pricing rationale deck for context.

Attachment: pricing_deck_q1.pdf
Jira: https://redwood.atlassian.net/browse/DEAL-9472

Karthik Iyer
Head of Deal Desk | Redwood Inference
